brief_item.title: TensorCast用张量即服务层解耦LLM推理张量管理
brief_item.direction_name: KVCache感知的网络与带宽调度
brief_item.core_conclusion: LLM系统把权重加载与KV放置等任务各自硬耦合在引擎里形成孤岛，TensorCast用张量即服务层将生命周期与计算解耦，使路由与KV放置可联合编程。
brief_item.mechanism: 用一等张量抽象与生命周期原语把张量管理从计算引擎解耦，分布式张量池统一调度放置与物化。
brief_item.result: RDMA下KV检索TTFT降60到87.5%与Mooncake持平，非RDMA场景明显更优。
brief_item.boundary: RDMA下仅与Mooncake持平，缺TPOT和P95且为预印本。
brief_item.project_relevance: 可借鉴其把路由与KV放置联合编程的思路，但应要求其给出绝对尾延迟与训练侧数据再决定跟进。

facts.title: TensorCast: The Missing Tensor Management Layer in Large Language Model Infrastructure
facts.event_hint: arXiv preprint (2608.06007v1, 6 Aug 2026) proposing TensorCast / Tensor-as-a-Service (TaaS), a distributed tensor lifecycle management layer for LLM infrastructure, integrated with vLLM and SGLang.
facts.problem: Existing LLM systems optimize individual tensor management tasks (weight loading, KV cache placement/transfer, checkpoint sync) by deeply coupling task-specific mechanisms with execution engines, networks, or storage backends, creating isolated silos that prevent reuse/composition and block cross-component optimizations such as jointly balancing instance load and KV cache locality.
facts.mechanism: A Tensor-as-a-Service (TaaS) layer decouples tensor lifecycle management from computation: first-class tensor abstractions (system-owned Artifact, caller-leased tensors), programmable lifecycle primitives (identify/place/materialize/transform_into/coordinate), a distributed tensor pool plus lifecycle runtime that separates policies from execution mechanisms, and an instance adaptor that confines engine-specific import/export. Uses view() for rank-specific slicing/resharding, CUDA IPC zero-copy for warm materialization (vLLM consumes pre-materialized tensors via tensor_dict in under 1 second), and a userspace mTCP implementation with multipath transmission for non-RDMA KV transfer.

evidence.claim: TensorCast accelerates large-tensor materialization in two scenarios. (a) Model weight synchronization (RL training-serving sync): 1.61x-2.00x for Qwen3-14B and 1.14x-2.63x for Qwen3-32B vs the Default JFS updater across TP=1/2/4 (Fig. 7). (b) MaaS instance launch (single-node, 8xH800, TP=8, safetensors from JuiceFS/SSD/tmpfs): under JFS for Qwen3-30B-A3B, TensorCast-cold cuts weight-load time by 60.7x vs Default and 10.2x vs InstantTensor, and end-to-end launch-ready time by 28.5x and 5.4x; TensorCast-warm (CUDA IPC prefetch) consumes weights in <1s, yielding 228.6x and 40.7x end-to-end launch speedups over Default and InstantTensor for Qwen3-235B-A22B (Fig. 5/6).
evidence.value: sync 1.14x-2.63x; launch cold 60.7x/10.2x load & 28.5x/5.4x ready; launch warm 228.6x/40.7x ready
evidence.baseline: Default (native vLLM loader / JFS updater) and InstantTensor fast weight loader
evidence.condition: Sync: 2-node, 64 CPU, 500GB DRAM, 4xH800, RDMA disabled for fairness, Qwen3-14B/32B. Launch: single node, 64 CPU, 500GB DRAM, 8xH800, vLLM TP=8, weights in safetensors from JuiceFS / node-local SSD / tmpfs.
evidence.source_locator: Sec 6.1 Setup/Results + Fig 5/6 (instance launch) and Sec 6.2 + Fig 7 (weight sync), PDF Page 11-12

evidence.claim: For Qwen3-32B (TP=2) KV cache retrieval, with RDMA enabled TensorCast achieves TTFT reductions of 60% to 87.5% (2.5x to 8x speedup) comparable to Mooncake, and significantly outperforms Mooncake with RDMA disabled.
evidence.value: 60% to 87.5% TTFT reduction (2.5x-8x speedup) with RDMA
evidence.baseline: State-of-the-art Mooncake KV-centric integration in SGLang under identical settings
evidence.condition: N-node cluster; each node 64 CPU, 1 TB DRAM, 8 x H800 GPUs, 200 Gbps RDMA links; LongBench prompts (~16k and ~35k tokens); 100% cache-hit rate stress test; TTFT reduction measured for N-1 instances relative to first instance.
evidence.source_locator: Section 6.3 'High-Cardinality Tensor Management', Results paragraph (Fig. 8a-8d), PDF Page 12-13.

evidence.claim: For Qwen3-235B-A22B (TP=8), TensorCast is comparable to Mooncake under RDMA and better without RDMA; TP=8 introduces 4x more concurrent KV page retrieval requests than TP=2, increasing contention and reducing TTFT improvements for both systems.
evidence.baseline: Mooncake KV storage backend in SGLang
evidence.condition: Same N-node H800 cluster; TP=8; 16k/35k token prompts; Fig. 9a-9d.
evidence.source_locator: Section 6.3, Results (Fig. 9), PDF Page 13.

evidence.claim: A programmable request-routing policy implemented with TensorCast (cache-aware routing plus KV-cache-migrating load rebalancing) improves median TTFT by up to 93.2% under highly concurrent multi-turn agent workloads.
evidence.baseline: Compared against Load-aware, Load-aware+Mooncake, and Cache-aware router policies (Fig. 10)
evidence.condition: Highly concurrent multi-turn agentic coding workloads; three LogNorm inter-turn delay presets (fast/medium/slow, Table 3); exact comparison cell and session count not restated in visible text.
evidence.source_locator: Abstract (PDF Page 1); Section 6.4 'Programmable Request Router' and Fig. 10/11 (PDF Page 13-14).

evidence.claim: Agent workload presets use LogNorm-sampled inter-turn delays: fast (median 8.2s, P95 22.0s), medium (median 20.1s, P95 75.0s), slow (median 60.3s, P95 311s), representing tight coding-agent loops, typical SWE agents, and long research/planning agents respectively.
evidence.condition: Synthetic LogNorm sampling within a session used to drive the §6.4 router evaluation.
evidence.source_locator: Table 3 'The three inter-turn delay presets used by the LogNorm sampling within a session', PDF Page 13.

facts.evaluation_context: Hardware: 2-node and N-node clusters of H800 GPUs (4x or 8x per node), 64 CPUs, 500 GB-1 TB DRAM, 200 Gbps RDMA links; the instance-launch study (Sec 6.1) uses a single 8xH800 node (TP=8) with weights in safetensors from JuiceFS / node-local SSD / tmpfs. Baselines: Default JFS weight updater, InstantTensor fast loader, and Mooncake (SGLang KV backend). Models: Qwen3-14B, Qwen3-30B-A3B, Qwen3-32B, Qwen3-235B-A22B with TP=1/2/4/8. Datasets/workloads: LongBench prompts (~16k/35k tokens), 100% cache-hit KV-reuse stress test, MaaS instance-launch (cold/warm materialization), and simulated multi-turn agent sessions (LogNorm inter-turn delays). Integrations: vLLM and SGLang. Reported metrics are TTFT reduction ratios, weight-sync/launch speedups, and cache-hit rate vs session count; absolute TPOT, token throughput, end-to-end P95 TTFT, and network utilization are not reported.
facts.limitations: Evaluations cover inference workloads only; training-framework integration (Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed) is explicitly left as future work (Discussion, PDF Page 14). Authors explicitly disclaim that a general abstraction is inherently faster than every specialized implementation; under RDMA, TensorCast is only comparable (not superior) to Mooncake, with its advantage concentrated in the non-RDMA and composability cases. The headline 93.2% TTFT gain is conditioned on highly concurrent multi-turn agent workloads and a specific programmable policy; the exact comparison baseline and session count are not restated in the visible text, and the targeted supplement (Sec 6.1 instance launch) did not expose the §6.4 router detail either. The deployment-level metrics requested (absolute TPOT, token throughput, end-to-end P95 TTFT, network utilization) are still absent. Agent workloads use synthetic LogNorm-sampled delays rather than a production trace. This is an arXiv v1 preprint.
facts.project_relevance: Relevant to the KV-cache-aware network/scheduling question: TensorCast provides a composable layer where request routing, KV placement, and instance load can be jointly programmed, and it reports TTFT reductions and a 93.2% median-TTFT agent-workload gain. However, the visible evidence reports reduction ratios rather than absolute TPOT, token throughput, end-to-end P95, or network utilization, and the network-side value is mainly in the non-RDMA (mTCP multipath) and cross-component composition cases rather than beating specialized RDMA KV systems head-to-head. Treat as a systems/preprint signal on composability, pending absolute tail metrics and training-side validation.
source_notes: Primary source is an arXiv preprint (v1, 2608.06007v1, 6 Aug 2026); fetch_status=FETCHED and raw_fulltext_cache_hit=true, so primary_source_resolved=true.
Evidence pack spans abstract/intro (PDF Page 1-3) and evaluation sections 6.1-6.4 + Discussion (PDF Page 11-14); results locators cite specific figures/tables.

Sec 6.1 instance launch (PDF Page 11): TensorCast-cold 60.7x/10.2x weight-load and 28.5x/5.4x launch-ready speedups over Default/InstantTensor under JFS (Qwen3-30B-A3B); TensorCast-warm 228.6x/40.7x launch-ready for Qwen3-235B-A22B via CUDA IPC zero-copy.
Fig 7 (PDF Page 11) confirms weight-sync speedups: Qwen3-14B 2.00x/1.81x/1.61x and Qwen3-32B 1.14x/1.66x/2.63x across TP=1/2/4.
Authors affiliated with Peking University, Stepfun, and Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications; work partly done at Stepfun.

brief_item.title: Kairos让Prefill在Decode节点就地完成以删除跨节点KV传输
brief_item.core_conclusion: 解耦推理在突发负载下排队与KV传输占P95 TTFT近八成，把Prefill迁至空闲Decode节点既降时延又删传输。
brief_item.mechanism: 用分析式TBT模型估算迁后解码时延，仅当Decode路径不劣于原节点且仍在SLO内才偏转。
brief_item.result: 在2P2D A100上P95 TTFT最多降81%，SLO达成率升79%。
brief_item.boundary: 仅四卡小集群与单一MoE模型验证，未量化KV传输量也未处理前缀缓存。
brief_item.project_relevance: 这是GPU调度侧而非网络侧的优化，可作为规避KV传输的基准，不回答网络机制本身的不可替代价值。

facts.title: Towards Load-Aware Prefill Deflection for Disaggregated LLM Serving
facts.event_hint: Kairos: a load-aware prefill-deflection scheduler that runs deflected prefill in place on decode nodes to cut P95 TTFT up to 81% and eliminate inter-node KV-cache transfer in disaggregated LLM serving.
facts.problem: Disaggregated LLM serving runs prefill and decode on separate GPU pools, which creates a new asymmetry: under bursty, heavy-tailed workloads prefill nodes saturate and queue while decode nodes sit underutilized (decode is memory-bound with spare compute). On a 2P2D A100 cluster the authors show prefill execution is only 2-23% of P95 TTFT; the remaining 77-98% is prefill queue wait and inter-node GPU-to-GPU KV-cache transfer, both scheduling artifacts rather than compute limits. Prior disaggregated designs (Splitwise, DistServe, Mooncake, TetriInfer) assume a request stays on its prefill node until prefill completes and then ships its KV cache to a decode node, so they cannot exploit the spare compute on decode nodes.
facts.mechanism: Kairos is a proactive, time-aware prefill-deflection scheduler. For each queued request it estimates TTFT on the prefill node from current queue depth/order, and for every decode node sweeps candidate chunk-size sequences using an analytical TBT-safety model that predicts per-step decode latency from in-flight decode batch size, KV-cache occupancy, and added prefill chunk size (no live inference trials; one-time deployment-time profiling; no model changes). It deflects the request's prefill phase to a decode node when both (i) TBT safety holds (in-flight decode step latency stays within the TBT SLO tau, with margin beta) and (ii) projected decode-node TTFT is at most alpha times the prefill-node TTFT, where alpha >= 1 is a single operator-tunable knob (alpha=1 deflects only when the decode path is strictly faster). Algorithm 1 (PDF Page 9) formalizes this: build a TBT-safe chunk schedule per decode node via LargestSafe, pick the fastest feasible node, then deflect only if TTFT_dec(n*) <= alpha * TTFT_pf and TTFT_dec(n*) <= TTFT_slo (Eq. 7), else Keep. Deflected prefill runs as chunked-prefill steps interleaved with in-flight decode batches, so the prefill phase executes in place on the decode node and the inter-node KV-cache transfer is eliminated. Implemented on vLLM 0.18.1 (~2000 lines of Python); per-request scheduling overhead is below 1 ms at the prefill dispatcher.

evidence.claim: Prefill execution accounts for only 2-23% of P95 TTFT across the five workloads; the remaining 77-98% is prefill queue wait plus inter-node KV-cache transfer (e.g., Bursty: 840.8 ms prefill queue, 1,070.1 ms prefill exec, 2,175.6 ms KV transfer, 7,893.9 ms end-to-end P95).
evidence.baseline: Canonical 2P2D disaggregated serving (2 prefill + 2 decode nodes), no deflection
evidence.condition: Five production-derived workloads (LPLD/LPHD/HPLD/HPHD/Bursty); DeepSeek-V2-Lite; A100 80GB
evidence.source_locator: Section 3.1 Claim 2 and Table 3, PDF Pages 4-5

evidence.claim: Kairos reduces P95 TTFT by up to 81% and raises SLO attainment by up to 79% over state-of-the-art disaggregated schedulers; the Section 6 evaluation names the baselines as PD Disaggregation (DistServe-style [21]) and TaiChi [18], run on the Bursty trace over RPS 6-12 where Kairos holds P95 TTFT/TBT SLO up to 9 RPS while PD disaggregation and TaiChi fall out earlier. Routing cost <1 ms per request.
evidence.value: up to 81% P95 TTFT reduction; up to 79% higher SLO attainment; <1 ms routing; SLO held to 9 RPS
evidence.condition: Bursty trace; RPS 6-12; SLO P95 TTFT<=4s and P95 TBT<=70ms; DeepSeek-V2-Lite; 2P2D A100 cluster; vLLM 0.18.1 (exact RPS/alpha of the 81%/79% maxima not stated in supplement)
evidence.source_locator: Abstract and Section 1, PDF Pages 1-2; Section 6.1.2 Baselines and 6.2/Figure 4, PDF Page 9

evidence.claim: Utilization is complementary: prefill SM utilization is 75-84% while decode SM utilization never exceeds 27%; the gap is widest in HPLD (84% prefill vs 7.5% decode), confirming decode-side compute slack available for chunked prefill.
evidence.condition: Five workloads; A100 80GB; measured via NVIDIA Nsight Systems
evidence.source_locator: Section 3 Claim 1 and Table 2, PDF Pages 3-4

evidence.claim: Injecting chunked prefill into decode batches keeps decode step-latency increase within 30 ms for chunk sizes up to 512 tokens across all workloads and batch sizes; for chunk sizes >= 1024 the first-chunk increase reaches about 30 ms (low-prefill regimes) up to about 50 ms (bursty/high-prefill regimes), so using large first chunks requires knowledge of cached-token volume.
evidence.value: delta T_step <= 30 ms for chunk size <= 512; up to ~50 ms for >= 1024
evidence.baseline: Decode step latency with no chunked-prefill injection
evidence.condition: Mixed prefill-decode batches on decode nodes across the five workloads
evidence.source_locator: Section 3 and Figure 1, PDF Page 5

evidence.claim: Deflected requests execute prefill in place on the decode node, eliminating the inter-node KV-cache transfer; the system needs only one-time deployment-time profiling, no model changes, and imposes less than 1 ms per-request scheduling overhead (~2000 lines of Python on vLLM 0.18.1).
evidence.value: inter-node KV transfer eliminated for deflected requests; <1 ms routing; ~2000 LoC
evidence.baseline: Canonical disaggregated serving ships KV cache from prefill node to decode node
evidence.condition: Kairos on vLLM 0.18.1; 2P2D A100; deflected requests only
evidence.source_locator: Sections 1-2 Contributions and Design, PDF Pages 1-2; Algorithm 1, PDF Page 9

facts.evaluation_context: Section 6 evaluation runs on Azure Machine Learning Compute Clusters using Standard_ND96amsr_A100_v4 nodes, each with 8x NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB GPUs via NVLINK 3.0, AMD EPYC 7V12 64-core CPU, 900 GiB host memory; inter-node communication over InfiniBand and Azure Accelerated Networking. Topology is 2 prefill + 2 decode nodes (2P2D), with prior 1P3D / 3P1D comparisons on the Bursty workload. Model: DeepSeek-v2-Lite (MoE, 16B total / 2.4B active). Section 6 evaluates on the Bursty trace (most realistic, non-stratified) over RPS 6-12. SLO targets (both simultaneous): P95 TTFT <= 4 s, P95 TBT <= 70 ms. Section 6 baselines: PD Disaggregation (traditional DistServe-style [21], all prefill on prefill nodes) and TaiChi [18] (unified aggregation/disaggregation with differentiated GPU instances and flowing-decode scheduling). Q1 result: Kairos holds SLO up to 9 RPS while PD disaggregation and TaiChi fall out earlier. Per-request routing <1 ms; heartbeat interval = 100 ms; the decode-side single-deflection-per-heartbeat bottleneck requires RPS >= |decode nodes| / heartbeat (~20), far above the SLO-supported RPS, and is extensible by scaling decode nodes. Traces derived from a large-scale production LLM serving deployment (Company X); five workloads as in Table 1.
facts.limitations: The headline 'up to 81% TTFT / 79% SLO attainment' are best-case figures from the abstract/contributions; Section 6 confirms the baselines (PD Disaggregation/DistServe-style and TaiChi) and the Bursty/RPS 6-12 condition but does not state the exact alpha or RPS at which the 81%/79% maxima occur, and at lower request rates Kairos behaves similarly to standard PD disaggregation (little gain). Evaluated on a single small cluster (2P2D, four A100 nodes) and a single model architecture (DeepSeek-V2-Lite, MoE); the full throughput-vs-RPS curve (Figure 5) and any pool sizes beyond 2P2D are not in the supplement. Benefit depends on decode-side compute slack and workload regime, and using chunk size >= 1024 for the first chunk requires cached-token-volume awareness. New caveat from supplement: if a request has a prefix already cached on a prefill node, deflecting it to a decode node loses that cached prefix, and Kairos currently does NOT account for prefix-cache residency in its TTFT estimate. The evidence reports GPU SM/TC/HBM utilization but not aggregate KV-cache bytes transferred or network-bandwidth utilization as outcome metrics; KV-transfer reduction remains stated qualitatively (eliminated per deflected request), not quantified.
facts.project_relevance: Directly relevant to the TPN/KV-transfer topic: Kairos is a per-request, KV-cache-occupancy-aware scheduler that eliminates inter-node KV-cache transfer for deflected requests by running prefill in place on decode nodes, and it reports end-to-end P95 TTFT (up to 81% lower) and SLO attainment, which the topic values. Important boundary for project inference: Kairos is a GPU-pool/scheduling-side mechanism, not a network-side optimization; it avoids KV transfer rather than making the network faster, so it illustrates what scheduling alone can achieve and does not answer the topic's question about the irreplaceable value of network-side mechanisms. The visible evidence does not report network utilization, KV-transfer bytes, or TPOT as improved outcome metrics.
source_notes: Primary arXiv PDF (2607.02043v1) fetched; evidence covers abstract, intro/design (Pages 1-2), empirical study with Tables 1-3 and Figure 1 (Pages 3-5), and a partial throughput result (Page 10).
System is named Kairos in the body; the abstract describes it as a proactive prefill-deflecting scheduler.

Repair supplement (PDF Pages 9, 11, 12) added Algorithm 1 (deflection decision), Section 6 setup/baselines (PD Disaggregation = DistServe-style [21]; TaiChi [18]), the Bursty RPS 6-12 eval with Kairos holding SLO to 9 RPS, the decode-bottleneck threshold (RPS >= |decode nodes|/heartbeat ~20), and the prefix-cache-residency-loss caveat. It did not state the exact alpha/RPS of the 81%/79% maxima, did not show the Figure 5 throughput curve, and did not quantify KV-transfer bytes/network utilization.

evidence_gaps.question: Which specific disaggregated scheduler is the baseline for the up-to-81% TTFT and up-to-79% SLO-attainment results, and under which workload, RPS, and alpha are those maxima achieved (versus non-bursty or lower-load cases)?

Does the paper quantify the KV-cache transfer reduction (bytes or transfers eliminated) or network-bandwidth utilization as an outcome, rather than only stating per-deflected-request elimination and GPU SM/TC/HBM utilization?

What is the full throughput-vs-RPS curve (Figure 5 text is truncated at '7 RPS'), and at what load or cluster scale do Kairos gains over PD disaggregation vanish; are results shown beyond 2P2D / four A100s?

brief_item.title: HBF首个开放标准公布，瞄准HBM与SSD之间的新层级

brief_item.mechanism: 规范采用8层或16层NAND堆叠与UCIe互连，并定义封装、电气和软件I/O要求。
brief_item.result: 公布规格覆盖最高512GB容量，三级带宽目标约为0.4至3.0TB/s。
brief_item.boundary: 目前仅有标准规格，尚无量产器件、真实负载或独立验证。

facts.title: SK hynix Unveils First HBF Standard Specifications with SanDisk at FMS 2026
facts.event_hint: SK hynix and SanDisk released the first open standard specifications for High Bandwidth Flash (HBF) via OCP, announced at FMS 2026 (Santa Clara, Aug 4-6, 2026); HBF is positioned as a new memory layer between HBM and SSDs for AI inference.
facts.problem: AI inference is driving a surge in data volumes to process, creating simultaneous memory-bandwidth and capacity-scalability bottlenecks that existing HBM (high bandwidth, limited capacity) and SSD (high capacity, lower bandwidth) layers each only partially address.
facts.mechanism: High Bandwidth Flash (HBF) is positioned as a new memory layer between HBM and SSDs: it leverages NAND die stacking to deliver HBM-like high-speed data transfer while significantly expanding capacity beyond what HBM provides. The standard adopts the UCIe industry-standard die-to-die interconnect so HBF can integrate across processor types (GPUs, CPUs), and it defines connection interfaces/electrical characteristics, reliability and packaging guidelines for the HBF die-stack process, and software I/O guidelines. The specification was published as an open standard through the Open Compute Project (OCP).

evidence.claim: HBF capacity specifications cover up to 512GB, based on two stack configurations (8-high and 16-high NAND dies).
evidence.condition: Announced standard specification (8-high / 16-high NAND die stacks); not a measured shipping device
evidence.source_locator: Spec paragraph: 'Capacity specifications cover up to 512GB based on two stack configurations (8-high and 16-high NAND dies)'

evidence.claim: HBF bandwidth is categorized into three grades (Grade1-3), delivering scalable performance from approximately 0.4TB/s to 3.0TB/s.
evidence.condition: Announced standard specification across Grade1~3; spec target, not an independent measured result
evidence.source_locator: Spec paragraph: 'Bandwidth is categorized into three grades (Grade1~3), delivering scalable performance from approximately 0.4TB/s to 3.0TB/s'

evidence.claim: HBF adopts the UCIe industry-standard interconnect, laying the groundwork to integrate HBF across different processor types including GPUs and CPUs.
evidence.condition: Standard specification; processor-portability is a stated design intent
evidence.source_locator: Interconnect paragraph: 'HBF technology adopts UCIe ... to flexibly integrate ... across different processor types, including GPUs and CPUs'

evidence.claim: HBF is positioned as a new memory layer between HBM and SSDs, enabling high-speed data transfer similar to HBM while significantly expanding capacity by leveraging NAND technology, targeting AI inference bandwidth and capacity bottlenecks.
evidence.condition: Vendor positioning statement; no quantitative HBM-vs-HBF comparison visible in the evidence pack
evidence.source_locator: HBF technology paragraph: 'a new memory layer between HBM and SSDs ... high-speed data transfer similar to HBM while significantly expanding capacity by leveraging NAND technology'

evidence.claim: The HBF standard was disclosed as an open standard through the Open Compute Project (OCP); the consortium launched ~February 2026 after the initial SK hynix-SanDisk standardization partnership in August 2025, with Google and Tenstorrent currently participating.
evidence.condition: Open standard via OCP; consortium status as of Aug 4, 2026 announcement
evidence.source_locator: OCP/consortium paragraphs: 'disclosed through the Open Compute Project (OCP) ... about six months after launching the consortium in February ... Google and Tenstorrent currently participating'

facts.evaluation_context: This is a vendor product/standardization announcement (SK hynix newsroom), not an experimental or system-evaluation paper. No measured benchmarks, no real-workload results, no independent validation in the evidence. Visible quantitative specs: capacity up to 512GB (8-high/16-high NAND stacks); bandwidth ~0.4-3.0 TB/s across three grades; UCIe interconnect. Venue: FMS 2026, Santa Clara Convention Center, Aug 4-6, 2026. Standardization timeline: SK hynix-SanDisk partnership Aug 2025, consortium launch Feb 2026, spec unveiling Aug 4, 2026.
facts.limitations: The announcement discloses standard specifications, not a mass-produced, sampled, or deployed product; per the project-context card, announced specs must be distinguished from sampling, mass production, and scale deployment, and these spec numbers should not be read as measured device capabilities. The evidence pack contains no access latency, P/E endurance, write amplification, power draw, cost/bit, or system-level / real-workload performance data. Headline comparative claims referenced in discovery (roughly 2.5x power-efficiency gain over a prior generation and ~540x capacity vs HBM) are NOT present in the visible Evidence Pack and are therefore not recorded as facts. No independent third-party validation; the source is a vendor newsroom/marketing release.
facts.project_relevance: HBF directly addresses the storage-media topic's question of whether a new non-volatile medium can shift the AI memory hierarchy boundary: it is an OCP open standard for a NAND-stacked, UCIe-interfaced layer sitting between HBM and SSDs, with concrete capacity (up to 512GB) and bandwidth (0.4-3.0 TB/s) specs. It is relevant to judging whether media innovation is moving from device metrics toward system usability, but the visible evidence only reaches the announced-standard stage, not measured system value. For the project, the open-standard + UCIe + multi-vendor-consortium framing (SK hynix, SanDisk, Google, Tenstorrent) is a deployment-ecosystem signal worth tracking, while power, endurance, latency, cost, and a clear mass-production timeline remain the gating unknowns. (Project inference, separate from source facts.)

facts.title: Kioxia and SanDisk 10th-Gen 332-Layer QLC NAND Achieves Industry's Highest Bit Density
facts.event_hint: Kioxia and SanDisk unveil 10th-generation 332-layer QLC 3D flash memory technology at FMS 2026 (Aug 4, 2026), claiming industry-highest QLC bit density.
facts.problem: AI training, inference, and hyperscale datacenter workloads are driving rapid data growth, pressuring storage to deliver higher capacity density, interface bandwidth, and power efficiency simultaneously within fixed power/cooling envelopes.
facts.mechanism: CMOS directly Bonded to Array (CBA) architecture fabricates CMOS logic and the memory array on separate wafers, then bonds them with high-precision wafer-to-wafer alignment; combined with a 332-layer optimized floorplan, Toggle DDR6.0 interface with Separate Command Address (SCA) protocol, and Power-Isolated Low-Tapped Termination (PI-LTT) for I/O data-out transfer power efficiency.

evidence.claim: 332-layer QLC 3D flash delivers up to 60% increase in bit density versus 8th-generation, achieving >37 Gb/mm^2.
evidence.condition: Vendor-stated spec from joint press release; QLC, 332-layer architecture with optimized floorplan.
evidence.source_locator: Section 'Key 10th-generation QLC 3D flash memory technology highlights' (first bullet); also stated in lead press release paragraph.

evidence.claim: First QLC 3D flash memory technology to reach a 4.8 Gb/s NAND interface, enabled by Toggle DDR6.0 and the Separate Command Address (SCA) protocol.
evidence.baseline: 8th-generation 3D flash memory (read/write bandwidth improved relative to it)
evidence.condition: 1 Gb/s calculated as 1,000,000,000 bits/s; value obtained under Kioxia/SanDisk specific test environment and may vary depending on use conditions.
evidence.source_locator: Section 'Key 10th-generation QLC 3D flash memory technology highlights' (second bullet); footnote 3 on 4.8 Gb/s test condition.

evidence.claim: CBA (CMOS directly Bonded to Array) architecture enhances density scaling, performance, and manufacturing efficiency.
evidence.condition: Each CMOS wafer and cell array wafer manufactured separately in optimized condition then bonded (footnote 2).
evidence.source_locator: Section 'Key 10th-generation QLC 3D flash memory technology highlights' (third bullet); footnote 2.

evidence.claim: PI-LTT (Power-Isolated Low-Tapped Termination) improves I/O data-out transfer power efficiency, addressing AI/cloud power and cooling challenges.
evidence.condition: No quantified percentage or absolute power figure given in the evidence.
evidence.source_locator: Section 'Key 10th-generation QLC 3D flash memory technology highlights' (fourth bullet); lead paragraph on power efficiency.

evidence.claim: Industry's highest bit density for QLC NAND benchmark, based on Kioxia and Sandisk survey as of August 3, 2026.
evidence.baseline: Industry QLC NAND (self-survey by Kioxia and Sandisk)
evidence.condition: Self-reported vendor survey, not an independent benchmark; 'benchmark 1' / 'industry's first' / 'industry's highest' are vendor claims.
evidence.source_locator: Lead paragraph ('setting the industry benchmark 1'); footnote 'As of August 3, 2026, based on Kioxia and Sandisk survey.'

facts.evaluation_context: Press-release technology announcement (not a benchmarked product). No workload, SSD-level throughput, latency, P/E endurance, write amplification, random I/O, absolute power draw, or cost/bit disclosed. Comparisons are to the companies' own 8th-generation; the 4.8 Gb/s interface figure is measured under an unspecified vendor test environment. Stage: unveiled at Future of Memory and Storage (FMS) 2026; Kioxia states it will 'accelerate development toward the commercialization' of 10th-gen QLC products.
facts.limitations: This is a vendor press release announcing technology, not a shipping product; no mass-production or sampling date, no device-level endurance (P/E cycles), no latency, no random bandwidth, no absolute power consumption, and no cost/bit are provided. All 'industry first/highest' claims rest on a Kioxia-SanDisk self-survey (as of Aug 3, 2026), not independent testing. The 4.8 Gb/s interface speed is explicitly noted to vary with use conditions. Read/write bandwidth improvement over 8th-gen is asserted but not quantified.
facts.project_relevance: Directly relevant to the NAND/Flash density-vs-system-value question: concrete generational density (>37 Gb/mm^2, +60%) and interface (4.8 Gb/s) gains are now claimed at the die level, but the evidence stops short of system-level metrics (endurance, latency, random I/O, absolute power, cost/bit, deployment timeline) needed to judge whether this moves QLC into a new tier of the AI storage hierarchy. Treat as a vendor roadmap/announce signal, not a deployable capability, pending commercialization and independent SSD/system benchmarks.
source_notes: Primary source is a Kioxia/SanDisk joint press release (vendor source level A, but marketing/announcement content).
Evidence pack is the vendor press release; no peer-reviewed or independent benchmark data present.
